question: In which of the following years was the Brahmo Samaj established by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1828**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828** in Kolkata, India.
 
• It aimed to reform Hindu society by discarding practices like **Sati, idolatry, and caste discrimination**.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was influenced by monotheistic principles and drew inspiration from the Upanishads.
 
• The organization advocated for **education, women's rights, and the abolition of social evils**.
 
• It played a critical role in the **Bengal Renaissance** and India's broader socio-religious reform movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy:**

 
 
• He is regarded as the "Father of Modern India" for his pioneering role in social and religious reform.
 
• He campaigned against the practice of **Sati** and was instrumental in its abolition in 1829.
 
• He strongly advocated for the **freedom of press** and modern education in India.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of Brahmo Samaj:**
 
 
• To promote monotheism and reject idol worship.
 
• To advocate for **universal brotherhood** and equality among all human beings.
 
• To encourage rational thinking and oppose superstitions.
 
 
 
• **Key Contributions of Brahmo Samaj:**
 
 
• It focused on **abolishing caste discrimination** and untouchability in Indian society.
 
• The organization supported **women’s education** and opposed child marriage and polygamy.
 
• It contributed to the establishment of educational institutions, including the **Hindu College (now Presidency University)** in Kolkata.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The Brahmo Samaj inspired various reform movements across India, including the **Prarthana Samaj** and the **Arya Samaj**.
 
• Its emphasis on rationalism and social justice continues to influence modern Indian thought and governance.
